document.title: Afghanistan: [Excised] Briefs the Ambassador on his Activities. Pleads for Greater Activism by U.N.
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Taliban File Update
document.note: [Confidential] Unidentified source describes activities supporting a peaceful resolution, including meetings in Tehran, in Dubai with Yunus Qanuni, and in Kandahar with Taliban ministers Mullah Hassan and Mullah Jalil. Ambassador Simons comments that Pakistan's claimed 20 million rupee aid to the Taliban through 1996 excluded Pak wheat and POL and the trucks and buses full of adolescent mujahid with a day or two of weapons training: 'Pakistan's real aid.'

events.description: Pakistani interlocutor's trip to Tehran Aug 4-5, discussions with Borujerdi
Meeting with Qanuni in Dubai
Meeting in Kandahar with Mullah Hassan and Mullah Jalil; proposal to split the political commission
Briefing of US Ambassador by the excised Pakistani official
Dispute within Pakistani government over wheat price for Afghanistan
Pakistani interlocutor met Masood in Farkhar; Masood professed friendship and promised to seek prisoner release.
Interlocutor went to Tehran, met Borujerdi and others, discussing shared objectives.
Interlocutor briefed Qanuni and pleaded for establishing a political commission; Qanuni agreed to drop Kabul demilitarization precondition.
Interlocutor met Mullah Hassan and Mullah Jalil in Kandahar, proposing a two-track political commission (ceasefire/prisoner exchange and future government).
Interlocutor's superior told him in late June to resolve the Afghan conundrum within one week, then relented to two weeks.
Pakistan faced problem over wheat pricing within its own government (Agriculture Ministry demanding 10 rupees/kg vs 6.5 in Peshawar).
US Ambassador met Pakistani interlocutor, discussed UN role, OIC vacant-seat policy, and Pakistani aid to the Taliban.
The briefer's last prior meeting with the US Embassy, covered in ref A.
The briefer visited Tehran (Aug 4-5). He met briefly with an Iranian official and had several discussions with Borujerdi.
The briefer met Qanuni in Dubai. He urged the Alliance to drop the Kabul demilitarization pre-condition, and Qanuni begged for speed from the GOP.

The briefer met Mullah Hassan and Mullah Jalil in Kandahar and proposed splitting the political commission into a ceasefire/prisoner exchange track and a future multi-ethnic government track. He had not received a response.
In early July the Taliban's stated pre-condition was reduced to release of the four 'peace emissaries' held by Malik. A week later they agreed to talk to Malik without pre-conditions.
The briefer made a side trip to Farkhar, where Masood professed friendship for Pakistan and promised to use his influence in Mazar to get the four prisoners released. The promise was never honored.
Brahimi's delayed arrival in Kandahar and his refusal to remain there threw off the schedule and prevented a planned meeting with Mullah Omar.
In the two days before Aug 27, tension shifted from Kabul to Kunduz, where Taliban blunders put the Alliance in a position to beat the Taliban.
The briefer briefed the US Ambassador and DCM on his mediation. He gave an analysis of the Northern Alliance and the GOP asked for US support of the OIC vacant seat policy.
The briefer planned to return to Kandahar in about ten days, where Mullah Omar was to receive him.

relationships.quote: WAR CRIMINALS, COMMUNIST STOOGES. AND GODLESS TRAITORS, SUCH AS AHMED SHAH MASOOD. GENERAL MALIK, AND BURHANUDDIN RABBANI.

relationships.detail: The Taliban consider Masood, Malik and Rabbani war criminals and traitors and reject their inclusion in a broad-based government.
relationships.quote: INCLUSION OF PEOPLE THEY CONSIDER WAR CRIMINALS, COMMUNIST STOOGES. AND GODLESS TRAITORS, SUCH AS AHMED SHAH MASOOD.

relationships.detail: The Taliban consider Malik a war criminal and traitor, though they offered to talk to him without pre-conditions.
relationships.quote: GODLESS TRAITORS, SUCH AS AHMED SHAH MASOOD. GENERAL MALIK, AND BURHANUDDIN RABBANI.

relationships.detail: The Taliban consider Rabbani a war criminal and traitor and reject inclusion of such figures in a broad-based government.
relationships.quote: GODLESS TRAITORS, SUCH AS AHMED SHAH MASOOD. GENERAL MALIK, AND BURHANUDDIN RABBANI.

relationships.detail: The two sides are in armed conflict, and mediation seeks a ceasefire, prisoner exchange and political commission.
relationships.quote: ONE TO WORK ON A CEASEFIRE AND EXCHANGE OF PRISONERS AND THE OTHER TO DISCUSS A FUTURE MULTI-ETHNIC [GOVERNMENT] FOR AFGHANISTAN.

relationships.quote: SHUTTLING BACK AND FORTH BETWEEN MAZAR AND KANDAHAR, WITH ONE SIDE TRIP TO FARKHAR... BOTH SIDES TO SOFTEN UP ON THE "IMPOSSIBLE" PRE-CONDITIONS

relationships.detail: The briefer pressed the Alliance to drop its pre-condition of demilitarizing Kabul.
relationships.quote: THE NORTHERN ALLIANCE REALIZED THAT IT COULD NOT FIRST DEMAND THE DE-MILITARIZATION OF KABUL

relationships.detail: The briefer is acting on behalf of the GOP, asking the US for support on his mediation and the OIC vacant seat policy.
relationships.quote: MADE A STRONG PLEA FOR GOP HELP TO GET THE PROCESS OF ESTABLISHING A POLITICAL COMMISSION UNDERWAY

relationships.detail: The GOP asked the US to support the OIC decision in favor of a 'vacant seat policy' toward Afghanistan at the UN.
relationships.quote: THE GOP ASKED US TO SUPPORT THE OIC DECISION IN FAVOR OF THE "VACANT SEAT POLICY" TOWARD AFGHANISTAN AT THE UN

relationships.detail: The OIC decided on a 'vacant seat policy' toward Afghanistan at the UN, as an incentive for the two sides to talk.
relationships.quote: OIC DECISION IN FAVOR OF THE "VACANT SEAT POLICY" TOWARD AFGHANISTAN AT THE UN, AS A WAY OF OFFERING THE TWO SIDES AN INCENTIVE

relationships.detail: The GOP believes UNSMA needs to be far more active in pushing the parties towards peace.
relationships.quote: IT ALSO BELIEVES THAT THE UNSMA NEEDS TO BE FAR MORE ACTIVE

key_claims: Pakistan has a privileged association with the Taliban but not control over them.
The US Ambassador argued Pakistani aid to Taliban exceeded the ISI's 20 million rupee figure, including wheat, POL, trucks and buses of adolescent mujahid with brief weapons training.
Pakistani interlocutor reported the Northern Alliance would collapse if the Taliban ceased military activity.
Taliban prisoner release demand was reduced from 100% to 30%, and the North dropped its demand to demilitarize Kabul.
Pakistan asked US to support the OIC 'vacant seat' policy at the UN.
Taliban considered 'broad-based government' anathema and prefer 'multi-ethnic government'.
